subject.title: fix(sqlite): normalize BLOB/TEXT type mismatches during STRICT migration

question: Should STRICT migration normalize and preflight all UNIQUE constraints, or is a generic rollback for secondary UNIQUE collisions an acceptable supported recovery policy?
rationale: This is a persisted-state and upgrade-recovery policy choice: extending preflight to arbitrary and partial unique indexes increases complexity, while keeping the present scope can leave a user at an opaque startup/doctor failure after type normalization.

options.title: Preflight all relevant uniqueness constraints
options.body: Extend the migration so normalized collisions in table UNIQUE constraints and unique indexes fail with the same actionable recovery guidance as primary-key collisions.

options.title: Accept transactional generic failures
options.body: Keep the primary-key-only scope, explicitly document the generic secondary-UNIQUE failure and a supported recovery route, and accept that those rare upgrades need operator intervention.

options.title: Pause for a dedicated migration design
options.body: Split this behavior into a narrower persisted-state migration proposal before merging the BLOB/TEXT normalization change.

recommendation.title: Preflight all relevant uniqueness constraints
recommendation.body: Extend the migration so normalized collisions in table UNIQUE constraints and unique indexes fail with the same actionable recovery guidance as primary-key collisions.

likelyOwner.reason: The related merged SQLite hardening work is the closest available historical ownership signal for the STRICT-migration recovery contract.
